elara_exp_model_challenged.title: A Useful Objection

traitEffects.note: The protagonist treats a scholar's claim as a model to test rather than an authority to obey.

elara_exp_model_challenged.interpretation: Instead of simply accepting Elara's expertise, the protagonist identifies an assumption worth testing, and Elara takes the objection seriously.

elara_exp_contradictory_footnote.title: The Contradictory Footnote

traitEffects.note: Contradictory evidence becomes a shared problem rather than an inconvenience to remove.

elara_exp_contradictory_footnote.interpretation: A marginal note contradicts the accepted chronology. Elara and the protagonist agree that the contradiction deserves investigation rather than dismissal.

elara_exp_tome_committed.title: A Model Put at Risk
elara_exp_tome_committed.interpretation: Elara puts one of her own published assumptions at risk by handing over the contradictory source and inviting a real test.

elara_exp_follow_evidence.title: Evidence Over Ownership

traitEffects.note: Both participants accept that a useful model must survive evidence, even when correction costs status or pride.

elara_exp_follow_evidence.interpretation: The evidence overturns Elara's published chronology. She accepts the correction because the work matters more than ownership of the old conclusion.

elara_exp_protect_consensus.title: Consensus Preserved

traitEffects.note: The protagonist understands the anomaly but chooses institutional safety over revision.

elara_exp_protect_consensus.interpretation: The contradiction is documented but not allowed to overturn the accepted model. Elara appreciates the caution but learns little about the protagonist as a research peer.

elara_exp_revision_mutual.title: Revision Is Mutual

traitEffects.note: Elara now breaks the protagonist's preferred revision, proving that reciprocal inquiry applies to both sides.

elara_exp_revision_mutual.interpretation: After correcting Elara, the protagonist becomes attached to the replacement theory. Elara finds the counterexample that forces the protagonist to revise in turn.

elara_exp_theory_neither_owned.title: A Theory Neither Owned

traitEffects.note: The working model is now genuinely co-produced; neither participant can treat the other as a passive assistant.

elara_exp_theory_neither_owned.interpretation: Elara and the protagonist build a third model from the failures of both earlier positions. The result belongs to the evidence more than to either author.

elara_exp_independent_verification.title: The Result Held Without Her

traitEffects.note: Independent verification is the decisive proof that evidence-first model revision has become the protagonist's own cognitive habit, even after an earlier cautious choice.

elara_exp_independent_verification.interpretation: Working alone on a separate archive problem, the protagonist follows contradiction instead of defending the first plausible model, then returns with a result Elara can independently reproduce.

elara_exp_resonance_scholarly_insight.title: Resonance: Scholarly Insight
elara_exp_resonance_scholarly_insight.interpretation: Essence stabilizes an evidence-first revision habit already demonstrated through reciprocal inquiry and independent verification.

elara_memory_footnote_won.title: The Footnote That Won
elara_memory_footnote_won.summary: A minor contradiction overturned a respected conclusion because both of you chose the evidence over ownership of the old model.
elara_memory_footnote_won.protagonistView: Expertise became more useful when it was allowed to lose an argument.
elara_memory_footnote_won.targetView: The collaborator cared enough about the work to challenge mine and remain after the correction became costly.

elara_memory_theory_neither_owned.title: A Theory Neither Owned
elara_memory_theory_neither_owned.summary: You built a model together only after evidence broke the versions each of you preferred.
elara_memory_theory_neither_owned.protagonistView: A collaborator who can overturn my model is more valuable than an assistant who confirms it.
elara_memory_theory_neither_owned.targetView: The relationship became intellectually reciprocal: correction could move in either direction.

elara_memory_result_held_without_her.title: The Result Held Without Her
elara_memory_result_held_without_her.summary: You reproduced the method on a problem Elara had never seen, then brought back a result she could independently verify.
elara_memory_result_held_without_her.protagonistView: The method no longer depended on Elara's presence or authority.
elara_memory_result_held_without_her.targetView: The collaborator had become a peer capable of producing falsifiable work independently.
